narrative.overview: RouteRoom feels like leaning over a beautifully made architectural model with a calm transit expert. Warm mineral surfaces make dense spatial information approachable; dark civic ink gives the interface authority; one vermilion route signal directs attention to the current decision.
keyCharacteristics: Map-first composition with a narrow decision rail.
Restrained mineral palette with one route signal.
Opaque tactile surfaces instead of glass.

rules.name: The One Route Signal Rule
rules.body: Vermilion occupies less than ten percent of the screen and always answers what is active now.

rules.name: The Geography Owns Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue belongs to water and geographic context, never generic buttons.

rules.name: The Model Table Rule
rules.body: Resting panels share one plane. If every panel casts a shadow, the hierarchy has failed.

dos: Do let the map occupy at least two-thirds of the main desktop workspace.
Do use Reicon consistently at 16px or 18px with Outline weight for interface actions.
Do animate ranking, focus, drawers, and confirmations with short GSAP transitions.
donts: Don't recreate a colorful low-poly toy city.
Don't rebuild a wall of equally weighted dashboard cards.
Don't add a generic AI chat bubble pasted over a normal route planner.
Don't use glassmorphism, purple gradients, neon accents, or ornamental data visualization.
